title: Utility PRDs
description: PRDs for 3-5 standalone utilities selected for testability. Each PRD covers all flags, exit codes, and stream behaviors derived from C source. Utilities: ts, wc, cat, sponge.

title: PRD: ts (timestamp stdin lines)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, moreutils source (ts.c), prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml

Write the PRD for ts following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. Derive all requirements from the moreutils C source (ts.c). The PRD must cover: reading stdin line by line and prepending a timestamp to each line; the default format string ('%b %e %T'); custom strftime format strings passed as arguments; -s flag (show elapsed time since ts started); -i flag (show incremental time between lines); -r flag (process existing timestamps, convert format); -m flag (use monotonic clock); high-precision sub-second suffixes when format includes %N or %.N. Exit-code contract: exit 0 on clean EOF, propagate non-zero from stdin pipeline signals. Reference binary: gts (Homebrew moreutils). Note in requirements which flags require timestamp normalization in differential tests.
acceptance_criteria: prd004-ts.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. Every flag from ts.c is covered as a numbered requirement. Differential testing normalization is noted for timestamp-containing output.

title: PRD: sponge (soak stdin and write to file)
description:
Type: documentation

Write the PRD for sponge following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. Derive all requirements from the moreutils C source (sponge.c). The PRD must cover: reading all of stdin into memory before opening the output file (this is the core contract: enables 'cmd | sponge file' where file is also cmd's input without truncating it mid-read); writing the buffered content to the named file after stdin closes; -a flag (append to file instead of overwriting); atomic replacement via a temp file and rename so the target is never partially written; writing to stdout when no filename is given (passthrough mode); exit code: 0 on success, non-zero on write failure. Explicitly state the large-input behavior: sponge must handle stdin larger than available memory by spilling to a temp file. Reference binary: gsponge (Homebrew moreutils).
acceptance_criteria: prd007-sponge.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. The soak-before-write contract is the first requirement. Temp-file atomic rename and large-input spill are covered. Exit-code contract is stated.

title: rel02.0 PRDs and Use Cases (ls core, du)
PRD: ls core (default, -1, -l, -a, -A, -d, --color, -h)
description:
Write the PRD for cmd/ls covering the core flag subset for rel02.0.

deliverable_type: documentation
format_rule: prd-format
release: rel02.0

Required reading:
- docs/specs/sources.yaml (ls entry: src/ls.c, main at line 1648, flag parsing at 1924)
- docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml (ls requires pkg/sys and pkg/format)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml (TerminalWidth, Stat/Lstat, SIGPIPE, SIGWINCH)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-format.yaml (Columns, FileTypeColor, HumanSize)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create:
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd008-ls.yaml

Required sections:
- id: prd008-ls
- title
- problem: why ls needs a Go implementation; macOS BSD ls vs GNU ls divergence; differential testing goal
- goals: G1-G5 (listing modes, filter, color, size, exit codes)
- requirements groups covering core scope only:
  R1: Default listing (multi-column on TTY via pkg/sys.TerminalWidth + pkg/format.Columns;
      single-column when stdout is not a TTY)
  R2: Single-column mode (-1) and long format (-l: permissions, nlinks, owner, group, size,
      mtime, name; uses pkg/sys.Stat for st_nlink/st_uid/st_gid; uses pkg/format.HumanSize for -h)
  R3: Filter flags (-a includes dotfiles, -A includes dotfiles except . and ..; -d lists
      directory entry itself without descending)
  R4: Color (--color=always|auto|never; auto suppresses when stdout not TTY via pkg/sys.IsTerminal;
      uses pkg/format.FileTypeColor for GNU LS_COLORS defaults)
  R5: Human-readable sizes (-h with -l; delegates to pkg/format.HumanSize binary mode)
  R6: Exit codes (0 success, 1 minor problems e.g. cannot access file, 2 bad option)
  R7: Signal handling (install SIGPIPE handler via pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler;
      install SIGWINCH handler via pkg/sys.OnTerminalResize to re-query column count)
- non_goals: -C, -x, -t, -S, -r, -U, -v, -i, -s, -n, -R, -F are deferred to prd010-ls-extended;
  --hyperlink, --dired, -Z (SELinux), --quoting-style, --block-size unit suffixes are out of scope
- acceptance_criteria: AC1 gls comparison for default/single-col/long, AC2 color suppression on
  non-TTY, AC3 -h sizes match gls -lh, AC4 diff test passes for all in-scope flags

Design decisions:
- ls requires both pkg/sys and pkg/format; this is the primary motivation for those packages
- Differential testing requires --color=never or normalizing ANSI codes; recommend running
  tests with --color=never by default and a separate color test with ANSI normalization
- Mtime fields in -l output vary by wall clock; normalization strategy: replace mtime column
  with MTIME placeholder (document this in the PRD acceptance criteria)
- Owner/group names vary by system; use -n (numeric IDs) for -l differential tests to
  eliminate this source of variance (note: -n is an extended flag deferred to prd010, so
  -l differential tests must use a fixture where owner UID=GID=0 or run as consistent user)

title: PRD: du (recursive directory sizes)
description:
Write the PRD for cmd/du against gdu.

deliverable_type: documentation
format_rule: prd-format
release: rel02.0

Required reading:
- docs/specs/sources.yaml (du entry: src/du.c, main at line 772, flag parsing at 808)
- docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml (du requires pkg/sys and pkg/format)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml (Stat/Lstat for st_blocks, st_dev, st_ino)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-format.yaml (HumanSize for -h)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml

Files to create:
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd009-du.yaml

Required sections:
- id: prd009-du
- title
- problem: macOS du vs GNU du divergence (block size defaults, flag behavior); differential testing
- goals: G1 recursive disk usage, G2 summary mode, G3 human-readable output, G4 all-files mode,
  G5 depth limiting, G6 grand total, G7 apparent size
- requirements groups:
  R1: Default behavior (recurse into each directory arg; print size + path for each subdirectory
      and the directory itself; block count in 1K units by default matching gdu default;
      uses pkg/sys.Stat for st_blocks accumulation)
  R2: Flag behavior:
    -h: human-readable sizes via pkg/format.HumanSize binary mode
    -s: summarize (print only the total for each argument, not subdirectories)
    -a: all files (print size for each file, not just directories)
    -d N / --max-depth=N: limit depth of recursion; -s is equivalent to --max-depth=0
    -k: report in 1K blocks (overrides default)
    -m: report in 1M blocks
    -c: print grand total line after all arguments
    --apparent-size: use file size (st_size) instead of block count (st_blocks)
  R3: Hard-link deduplication: files with the same st_dev + st_ino must be counted only once
      per du invocation (du.c:554 inode tracking). Uses pkg/sys.Stat for st_dev and st_ino.
  R4: Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error (cannot stat or read directory)
  R5: Differential testing: both binaries must run on the same directory fixture on the same
      filesystem; use -k to normalize block size units across platforms
- non_goals: --si (1000-based), --exclude, --exclude-from, -D (dereference only command-line
  symlinks), -L (dereference all symlinks), -l (count hard links multiple times),
  --time (show modification time), --inodes
- acceptance_criteria: AC1 gdu comparison on fixture directory with default flags, AC2 -s summary
  matches gdu -s, AC3 -h human sizes match gdu -h, AC4 hard-link dedup (one file hard-linked twice
  counts once), AC5 --apparent-size matches gdu --apparent-size, AC6 diff test passes

Design decisions:
- Block size default: gdu uses 1K blocks; du (macOS BSD) uses 512-byte blocks. Use 1K as default.
- Differential tests use -k to pin block unit and avoid platform divergence
- Hard-link tracking requires a map[uint64]map[uint64]bool (dev->ino->seen) per invocation
- pkg/sys.Stat is required (not os.Stat) to access st_blocks and st_ino/st_dev

title: Source Extraction
description: Clone and catalog the four C source repositories (coreutils, moreutils, grep, findutils). Produce a sources catalog and a shared-dependency map that identifies which pkg/ components each utility will need.

title: Clone source repositories and catalog utility locations
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: bootstrap-prompt.md, docs/VISION.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/sources.yaml

Clone the four C source repositories and catalog each utility's location within them. For each utility record: the source file(s), the flag-parsing entry point, where exit-code logic lives, and the Homebrew reference binary name (e.g. gts, gwc, gcat, gsponge, gpee, gls). Repositories to clone:
  - coreutils (ls, cat, cp, mv, wc, du): https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils.git
  - moreutils (ts, sponge, vidir, pee, chronic): https://git.joeyh.name/git/moreutils.git
  - grep (grep, egrep, fgrep): git://git.savannah.gnu.org/grep.git
  - findutils (find, xargs): git://git.savannah.gnu.org/findutils.git

Clone into a local scratch area (e.g. /tmp/sources/). Do not commit the cloned repos. Only commit docs/specs/sources.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: docs/specs/sources.yaml exists and maps every utility in the four repos to its primary source file and Homebrew reference binary name. All 14 utilities are covered.

title: Analyze source and produce shared-dependency map
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/specs/sources.yaml, docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml

Files to create: docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml

For each of the 14 utilities, analyze the catalogued C source and identify which shared pkg/ components it will need: pkg/testutils (all utilities), pkg/sys (ls, du, find, xargs -- file metadata, signals, terminal), pkg/format (ls, du -- table alignment, ANSI color, unit conversion). Note any shared behavioral patterns not yet reflected in ARCHITECTURE.yaml (e.g. shared exit-code conventions, shared option-parsing idioms). The dependency-map is the input that justifies the scope of each shared component PRD.

title: rel02.1 PRDs and Use Cases (ls extended)
PRD: ls extended (-C, -x, sort, -i, -s, -n, -F, -R)
description:
Write the PRD for cmd/ls extended flags, building on prd008-ls.
Depends on: main-7n8.1 (prd008-ls must exist first).

deliverable_type: documentation
format_rule: prd-format
release: rel02.1

Required reading:
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd008-ls.yaml (core PRD this extends)
- docs/specs/sources.yaml (ls entry: src/ls.c flag parsing at line 1924)
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-format.yaml

Files to create:
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd010-ls-extended.yaml

Required sections:
- id: prd010-ls-extended
- title: 'cmd/ls: Extended Flags'
- problem: prd008-ls covers core flags; the extended flags add multi-column layout control,
  sort order options, metadata display, file type indicators, and recursive listing.
  These require heavier output normalization in differential tests and more complex
  interaction with pkg/format.Columns and pkg/sys.Stat.
- goals: G1 multi-column layout control, G2 sort options, G3 metadata display, G4 classify, G5 recursive
- requirements groups:
  R1: Multi-column layout
    -C: force multi-column output even when stdout is not a TTY (uses pkg/format.Columns)
    -x: like -C but sorts entries horizontally (across columns) instead of vertically (down columns)
  R2: Sort order
    -t: sort by modification time, newest first (uses mtime from pkg/sys.Stat)
    -S: sort by file size, largest first (uses st_size from pkg/sys.Stat)
    -r: reverse the sort order (applies to whichever sort is active)
    -U: do not sort (directory order); disables all other sort flags
    -v: natural sort of version numbers within text (strverscmp semantics)
  R3: Metadata display
    -i: prepend inode number to each entry (uses st_ino from pkg/sys.Stat)
    -s: prepend allocated block count to each entry (uses st_blocks; same unit as du default)
    -n: in -l format, display numeric UID and GID instead of looking up names
    -F: append type indicator to each filename (/ dir, * executable, @ symlink, | pipe, = socket)
  R4: Recursive listing
    -R: recursively list subdirectories; print each subdirectory header as 'path:' before its contents
  R5: Interactions
    -n implies -l (activates long format with numeric IDs)
    -C and -x are mutually exclusive with -l and -1
    -R with -l: each subdirectory's contents listed in long format
- non_goals: --hyperlink, --dired, -Z, --quoting-style remain out of scope
- acceptance_criteria: AC1 -C output matches gls -C for fixture dir, AC2 -t sort matches gls -t,
  AC3 -i inode matches gls -i (after inode normalization), AC4 -R recursive matches gls -R,
  AC5 -n numeric IDs in -l matches gls -ln

Design decisions:
- -i output contains inode numbers that differ between test runs if fixture is recreated;
  differential tests normalize by running both binaries on same live filesystem, not by
  replacing inode values. Document this as a precondition.
- -s block counts: use same -k normalization as du differential tests
- -v (version sort) requires strverscmp semantics; implement in-house (no external library)

title: PRD: pkg/sys (syscall abstractions)
description:
Type: documentation

Required reading: docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml, docs/specs/dependency-map.yaml, coreutils source (src/ls.c, src/du.c), findutils source (find/find.c, xargs/xargs.c)

Files to create: docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml

Write the PRD for pkg/sys following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. The PRD must explain why sys is a shared component: ls, du, find, and xargs all need stat/lstat, device/inode access, and signal handling (SIGPIPE, SIGWINCH, SIGHUP), and Darwin vs Linux divergence is best managed once. For each syscall surface (file metadata, terminal size, signal handling), state which utilities drive it and what each utility needs from it. Requirements must cover: stat and lstat returning file mode, size, mtime, device, inode; terminal width query (for ls column layout); SIGPIPE handling (suppress broken-pipe errors on stdout close); SIGWINCH handling (re-query terminal width on resize).
acceptance_criteria: prd002-sys.yaml exists and passes mage analyze. Each requirement names the utilities that depend on it. Darwin/Linux portability is addressed in requirements or design decisions.

title: PRD: pkg/format (output formatting)
description:

Write the PRD for pkg/format following the prd format in docs/constitutions/design.yaml. The PRD must explain why format is a shared component: both ls and du produce tabular output with column alignment, ANSI color for file types, and human-readable size formatting (K/M/G/T), and duplicating this logic across cmd/ packages would produce inconsistent output. For each formatting capability (column alignment, ANSI color, unit conversion), state which utilities drive it and what each utility needs.
